FRONT COVER. The late Alfred A. Harley

The caption that goes with this photograph in our archives reads:
"Walk Match at Battersea circa 1938. Starters include H.G. Churcher, C.E.Churcher, D.E. Brown, A.A.Harley, F. Jarvis, C.W.Redgrave."
Our first stab at actually naming the faces came up with Don Brown (1), Harry Churcher (7), Charlie Churcher (23), C.W. Redgrave (24) and Alf Harley (behind Brown). However, as others have become involved and have cast their eyes over the picture, we are now not at all sure of anyone except Alf Harley. For instance, we are told that Charlie Churcher did not wear glasses and the chap next to Harry, second from the left, may be Jack Rutland If any reader can help us with more specific details of the race then we would be very pleased to hear from them.

* Edward Heath has his music - Alfred Harley has his amateur dramatics - here he is seen in, "Lockhart's Last Case" with a strong supporting cast. In the background it looks like Charlie MacLennan (without trousers) taking finger-prints and the immediate foreground are three heads waiting for the chop whilst the amiable assistant "Tinker" is being carpeted by the boss.
FRONT COVER---Our retiring General Hon. Secretary, ALF HARLEY, who vacates his Chair after a term of office spanning 32 years. See page 8.
Charlie Redgrave, "The Banjulele Boy", passes Alf Harley only feet from the tape to win the 1929 Boxing Day Walk Handicap.
Alf Harley (12) competing in the Chiswick Annual Sports----August 1933.

21st JUNE 1952. Five months after her accession to the throne HER MAJESTY QUEEN ELIZABETH II visits the A.A.A. Championships at the White City. On the left is A.A. Harley and to the right The Marquess of Exeter.

Another milestone in the life of ALF HARLEY is reached during the 1950's when, as Chairman of the London Association of Athletic Clubs, he receives the ROMULUS AND REMUS trophy from the Italians at London's Dorchester Hotel
